intro: Professionals and everyday users convert liters (L) to pints (us) (pt) when working across metric and us_customary standards in culinary recipe scaling, beverage bottling, laboratory reagent preparation, and fluid tank capacity sizing. One liter equals 2.113376 pints (us), while 1 pint (us liquid) equals 0.473176 liters. Whether you are verifying volume & liquid specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many pints (us) (pt) are in 1 liter (L)?
faqs.answer: There are 2.11337642 pints (us) (pt) in 1 liter (L), which rounds to 2.1134 pt for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pint (us liquid) equals 0.473176 liters.

faqs.question: How do I convert liters to pints (us) (L to pt)?
faqs.answer: To convert liters to pints (us), use the formula: pt = L × 2.11337642. For example, converting 1.5 L gives 3.1701 pt.

faqs.question: What is 1.5 liters in pints (us)?
faqs.answer: 1.5 liters (L) equals exactly 3.1701 pints (us) (pt) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
